chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgets to shave his head until he departs from Mina. He said: 'I do not like that he casts off his hair except in Mina, and he has not placed anything upon it.' The meaning in this report is that whoever does not do so is not obliged to pay expiation, except that he has left the preferable act.

key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: Expiation (penalty for missing a ritual act)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a plain near Mecca where pilgrims spend days of Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to shave their head before leaving Mina?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that forgetting to shave in Mina before departure does not impose a mandatory expiation (*kaffarah*), distinguishing between obligatory duties and recommended acts (*fada'il*). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that negligence in recommended acts, unlike obligatory ones, does not trigger penalty, thereby offering ease to pilgrims who may have missed the specific time or place for *halq*. The context highlights the flexibility within Hajj rituals, ensuring that the validity of the pilgrimage remains intact despite minor omissions in preferred practices.
